title: Word knowledge can't need the text
statement: A skill that is word knowledge, such as word parts, synonyms or connotation, can't be tested by a question that needs the text, so decide separately how to assess it.
example: With the passage hidden, a model answered 36 of 45 generated vocabulary items, every word-part, synonym and connotation item among them.
detail: A text-hidden check answered 36 of 45 generated vocabulary items, and every word-part, synonym and connotation item, because the skill is word knowledge rather than inference from the passage. The course plan concluded that those slots needed a fundamentally different design, or a decision that they cannot be tested as text-dependent items and should leave the comprehension blueprint. A later bank of 120 vocabulary seed items leaked 99.2% and was marked to be rewritten and re-certified, never used as it stood.
against: Context-clue items partly worked: 8 of 15 survived, those using words in technical or domain senses (`grade3-reading/artifacts/LANE1_COURSE.md`, line 240).

evidence.quote: Skill IS word-part knowledge, not passage inference — cannot be made passage-dependent.
cannot be tested as passage-dependent items and should be excluded from the comprehension-course blueprint
the 120 L.5 vocab seeds LEAK 99.2% and must be re-authored + re-certified, never deployed as-is
L.5 vocabulary items fail blind-solve at high rates (~99%) when the target word carries its common meaning and the student can guess from background knowledge alone.
**The correct answer must require a passage-specific context clue that overrides or narrows the word's common meaning.**
L.5 vocab 80% blind-solve leak (36/44 slots need redesign; some substandards may be inherently world-knowledge)
